Author: Segal et al.
Comment: The paper does not report final analyzed N by group for this fatigue contrast, so group Ns and total analyzed N are left null rather than using randomized Ns. M_diff is the paper-reported unadjusted RET-minus-UC difference in baseline-to-12-week mean change, not the difference between the two 12-week endpoint means. Title: Effects of high-intensity interval training compared with resistance training in prostate cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy: a randomized controlled trial
Author: Piraux et al.
Comment: The extracted means and SDs are the T1 endpoint values because Table 3 does not report SDs for change scores; the reported p=0.039 is the RES-versus-UC post-hoc comparison of pre-to-post change. FACIT-F is oriented higher = less fatigue, so the raw endpoint difference favors RES and must be oriented consistently with the review's convention that positive standardized effects favor resistance training. The Results narrative gives UC change as −5.3 points, whereas Table 3 gives −5.8 (95% CI −9.9 to −1.8); Table 3 was preferred. HIIT was excluded because it does not match the planned resistance-training intervention.
